gloss: be whole, complete; make whole, pay, repay; peace, welfare; peace offering
summary: To be whole, with nothing missing: a work finished, a weight full, a heart undivided toward Yahweh (1Ki 7:51; Deu 25:15; 1Ki 8:61). So the piel is to make whole what was lost or owed: restore what was stolen, pay a vow or a debt, and repay good or evil (Exo 21:37; Psa 50:14; Deu 32:35); and the hiphil is to make peace with an enemy (Jos 10:1). שָׁלוֹם is that wholeness in a life and between people: welfare (“is he well?”), safety, peace instead of war, the greeting “peace to you”, and the peace Yahweh gives and covenants (Gen 29:6; Ecc 3:8; Num 6:26). The שְׁלָמִים, peace offerings, were the sacrifice of which the offerer ate before Yahweh, offered when vows were paid (Lev 7:11–16; Pro 7:14).

words.summary: The state of being whole and well, in a body, a household, a city or between peoples. Asking after a man’s שָׁלוֹם is asking how he is; going in שָׁלוֹם is going unharmed; making שָׁלוֹם ends a war. Yahweh gives it, covenants it, and makes it, and the prophets promise it in the king to come.

senses.definition: How a person, a household or a city fares: whether all is well with them, sound and in order.

evidence.note: “Is he well (הֲשָׁלוֹם לוֹ)?” And they said, “Well (שָׁלוֹם).” Jacob asks after Laban.
Joseph asks his brothers of their שָׁלוֹם and says, “Is your father well (הֲשָׁלוֹם), the old man? Is he still alive?”
“See the welfare of your brothers and the welfare of the flock.”
“There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation; there is no שָׁלוֹם in my bones because of my sin”: the body whole.
“Seek the welfare of the city … for in its welfare you will have welfare.”
“Is it well with the young man Absalom?”
Mordecai walks before the court to know Esther’s welfare.
The Peshitta and Greek: the father received his son “safe and sound” (ὑγιαίνοντα), the Septuagint’s word for שָׁלוֹם in Gen 29:6.

senses.definition: Coming or going without harm, and so dying in old age without violence: “in שָׁלוֹם” is safe and sound.

evidence.note: Jacob’s vow: “if I return in peace to my father’s house”; he came back שָׁלֵם (Gen 33:18).
Ahab: feed him “until I come in peace”; Micaiah: “If you return at all in peace, Yahweh has not spoken by me” (22:28). Ahab died in the battle.
“When I come back in peace I will break down this tower.”
“You will go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.”
“Do not let his grey head go down to the grave in peace”: Joab’s death is not to be a quiet one.
Josiah to be gathered to his grave in peace, and not see the evil coming on the place.
“In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for you alone, Yahweh, make me dwell in safety (לָבֶטַח).”
Simeon in the Peshitta: “Now let your servant depart, my Lord, in peace (בַּשלָמָא)”, as Abraham was promised in Gen 15:15.

senses.definition: The state between peoples or persons when there is no war or enmity, and the terms on which a war ends.

evidence.note: “A time for war and a time for peace.”
“I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.”
“When you draw near a city to fight against it, call to it for peace”; if it answers peace and opens, it serves (20:11); if it will not make peace (הִשְׁלִים) but war, besiege it (20:12).
Joshua made peace with the Gibeonites and cut a covenant with them.
Solomon “had peace on all sides round about him”.
Peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two cut a covenant.
The congregation proclaimed peace to the Benjamites at the rock Rimmon.
“A man of rest … for שְׁלֹמֹה shall be his name, and peace and quietness (שָׁלוֹם וָשֶׁקֶט) I will give to Israel in his days”: Solomon named for it.

senses.gloss: friendship; one at peace with another
senses.definition: The bond of those who are at peace with one another: אִישׁ שְׁלוֹמִי, “the man of my peace”, is a trusted friend, and speaking peace to a neighbour is the outward sign of it.

evidence.note: “Even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.”
Jesus applies Psa 41:10 to Judas: “He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.”
“Your men of peace have deceived you and prevailed against you.”
“The men of your peace have deceived you.”
Those “who speak peace with their neighbours, but evil is in their hearts”.
“With his mouth one speaks peace to his neighbour, but in his heart he sets an ambush.”
Joseph’s brothers “could not speak to him in peace”.

senses.gloss: greeting: “peace to you”; asking after welfare
senses.definition: Wishing or asking שָׁלוֹם is the ordinary greeting: “peace to you” on meeting, “go in peace” at parting, and שָׁאַל לְשָׁלוֹם “ask after the welfare” of someone.

evidence.note: David’s message to Nabal: “Peace to you, and peace to your house, and peace to all that you have.”
“Go to Nabal, and ask him of peace (וּשְׁאֶלְתֶּם־לוֹ … לְשָׁלוֹם) in my name.”
The old man of Gibeah: “Peace to you.”
Moses and Jethro “asked each other of their welfare”.
Eli to Hannah: “Go in peace (לְכִי לְשָׁלוֹם).”
“Is it peace, Jehu?” “What peace, while the whoredoms of your mother Jezebel …?”
“Fear not, man greatly loved; peace to you.”
Jesus: “Into whatever house you enter, first say, Peace to this house”: David’s greeting of 1Sa 25:6.
The Peshitta: “ask the peace (שַאלו שלָמֵה) of the house”, the Hebrew idiom.
“Your faith has saved you; go in peace”, Eli’s words to Hannah.
The risen Jesus: “Peace to you.”

senses.gloss: peace given by Yahweh; his covenant of peace
senses.definition: The wholeness and peace that Yahweh gives his people, binds himself to by covenant, and withholds from the wicked; promised in the king and servant to come.

evidence.note: The priests’ blessing: “Yahweh lift up his face to you and give you peace.”
“Behold, I give him my covenant of peace”: to Phinehas.
“The mountains may depart … but my kindness shall not depart from you, nor my covenant of peace be removed.”
“I will cut a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant.”
“I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down and none shall make you afraid.”
“Yahweh will bless his people with peace.”
“The mind stayed on you you will keep in peace, peace, because it trusts in you.”
“There is no peace, says Yahweh, for the wicked”; again Isa 57:21.
“The chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed.”
The child born to us is called שַׂר־שָׁלוֹם, Prince of Peace; “of the increase of his government and peace there is no end” (9:6).
“Peace, peace, to the far and to the near”, quoted in Eph 2:17.
Christ “came and preached peace to you who were far off and to those who were near”.
“We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.”
“Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.”

senses.definition: The cry of the false prophets that all is well when judgment is coming.

evidence.note: “They have healed the hurt of my people lightly, saying, Peace, peace, when there is no peace”; again Jer 8:11.
“They have misled my people, saying, Peace, and there is no peace”: a wall daubed with whitewash.
Prophets who “cry Peace” while they have something to eat, and declare war on whoever feeds them nothing.
“When they say, Peace and safety, then sudden destruction comes upon them.”

evidence.locator: Num.6.26, שָׁלוֹם → εἰρήνην; Isa.53.5, שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ → εἰρήνης; εἰρήνη renders שָׁלוֹם ×176

evidence.note: Isa 59:8 quoted: “the way of peace they have not known”.
Psa 34:15 quoted: “let him seek peace and pursue it”.
Isa 52:7: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the gospel of peace.”
Isa 57:19: peace to the far and the near.
“King of Salem, which is, king of peace”: שָׁלֵם read as שָׁלוֹם.
πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην, the Septuagint’s words for “go in peace” in 1Sa 1:17.

evidence.locator: Gen.29.6, הֲשָׁלוֹם … שָׁלוֹם → ὑγιαίνει; Gen.43.27 the same

evidence.note: The son received back “safe and sound” (ὑγιαίνοντα).
“That you may prosper and be in health (ὑγιαίνειν).”

parallels.note: “Righteousness”, set beside peace in the kingdom and as its source.

evidence.note: “Righteousness and peace have kissed.”
“The work of righteousness shall be peace.”
“Love truth and peace.”

parallels.note: “Good”, beside peace in the one pursued and in the news proclaimed.

evidence.note: “Depart from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.”
“Who proclaims peace, who brings good news of good.”

opposites.note: “Evil, calamity”: what Yahweh brings instead of peace.

evidence.note: “Making peace and creating evil.”
“Thoughts of peace and not of evil.”

phrases.gloss: ask after the welfare of; greet
the man of my peace: a trusted friend

words.gloss: be whole, complete; make whole, restore, pay, repay; make peace
words.summary: The qal is to be whole or finished, and to be at peace with someone. The piel, nine uses in ten, is to make whole: to restore in full what was stolen or damaged, to pay a vow or a debt, and to repay a man for what he has done, good or evil, which Yahweh claims as his own. The hiphil is to make peace with an enemy, or to bring a purpose to completion.

stems.gloss: be whole, finished; be at peace

senses.definition: Of a work, brought to its end with nothing left undone; of days, run out; of a man, kept whole and unharmed.

evidence.note: “So all the work that Solomon did for the house of Yahweh was finished.” Again 2Ch 5:1.
“So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in fifty-two days.”
“The days of your mourning shall be ended.”
“Who has hardened himself against him and remained whole (וַיִּשְׁלָם)?”

senses.definition: To be at peace with someone, or to come to peace with God; the participle is one at peace with another.

evidence.note: “Acquaint yourself now with him and be at peace (וּשְׁלם); thereby good will come to you.”
“If I have repaid evil to him who was at peace with me (שׁוֹלְמִי).”
The wise woman of Abel: “I am of the peaceable (שְׁלֻמֵי), the faithful of Israel.”

stems.gloss: make whole, restore; pay; repay, requite; finish

senses.definition: To make good a loss: to restore what was stolen, killed or damaged, so that the owner is whole again; and of God, to restore what was lost.

evidence.note: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills or sells it, he shall restore five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.”
Grazing another’s field: “of the best of his own field … he shall make restitution.”
A borrowed beast that dies: “he shall surely make it good.”
The owner of the pit “shall make it good”.
What was taken by deceit: “he shall restore it in full (בְּרֹאשׁוֹ) and add a fifth to it”.
“He who kills a beast shall make it good, life for life.”
David: “he shall restore the lamb fourfold”.
The wicked who turns “restores the pledge, gives back what he had robbed”.
“I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten.”
“He will make whole (וְשִׁלַּם) the habitation of your righteousness.”
“I will lead him and restore comforts to him and to his mourners.”

senses.definition: To pay in full what is owed: a vow made to God, or a debt to a man.

evidence.note: “Offer to God thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High.”
“When you vow a vow to Yahweh your God, you shall not delay to pay it.”
“Pay what you vow. Better that you should not vow than vow and not pay” (5:4).
“I will pay my vows to Yahweh now in the presence of all his people.”
“What I have vowed I will pay. Salvation is of Yahweh.”
“Peace offerings are with me; today I have paid my vows”: the vow paid with שְׁלָמִים.
“Keep your feasts, Judah, pay your vows.”
Elisha to the widow: “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt.”
“The wicked borrows and does not pay back.”
“You shall perform (ἀποδώσεις; Peshitta תּשַלֵם) to the Lord your oaths.”

senses.definition: To give a man back the equivalent of what he has done: good for good, evil for evil, or evil for good. Yahweh repays every man according to his work, and claims recompense as his own.

evidence.note: “Why have you repaid evil for good?”
“To you, Lord, belongs kindness, for you repay each man according to his work”; Rom 2:6.
“Yahweh repay your work, and may your reward be full (שְׁלֵמָה)”: the verb and the adjective together.
“Do not say, I will repay evil; wait for Yahweh, and he will save you.”
Feed your enemy, “and Yahweh will reward you”; Rom 12:20.
“He who is gracious to the poor lends to Yahweh, and he will repay him his deed.”
“I will return vengeance to my adversaries and repay those who hate me.”
Adoni-bezek: “As I have done, so God has repaid me.”
“They repay me evil for good.”
Saul to David: “Yahweh reward you with good.”
“Yahweh is a God of recompenses; he will surely repay.”
“I will not keep silent, but will repay, repay into their bosom.”
“Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is mine”; Rom 11:35.
Paul gives Job 41:3 from the Hebrew: “Who has first given to him, and it shall be repaid him?”
“Repay no one evil for evil.”

senses.definition: To bring a work to its completion.

evidence.note: Solomon offered three times a year on the altar he built, “and he finished (וְשִׁלַּם) the house”.

stems.gloss: be paid, be repaid; (participle) one at peace

senses.definition: Of a vow, to be paid; of a man, to be repaid for what he has done.

evidence.note: “To you shall the vow be paid.”
“Shall evil be repaid for good? For they have dug a pit for my life.”
“The righteous will be repaid on the earth; how much more the wicked and the sinner.”
“He who fears the command will be rewarded.”

senses.definition: Once, of Yahweh’s servant: מְשֻׁלָּם, beside “my servant” and “the servant of Yahweh”; whether “one at peace (with God)”, “one made whole”, or “one paid for”, the verse does not settle.

evidence.note: “Who is blind but my servant, or deaf as my messenger whom I send? Who is blind as מְשֻׁלָּם, and blind as the servant of Yahweh?”

stems.gloss: make peace with; complete, carry out

senses.definition: To end hostilities with an enemy by coming to terms, usually by submitting to the stronger.

evidence.note: “If it will not make peace with you, but makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.”
“The inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them.”
“There was not a city that made peace with the sons of Israel except the Hivites of Gibeon.”
Hadadezer’s vassals “made peace with Israel and served them”.
“Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.”
“When a man’s ways please Yahweh, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.”

senses.gloss: carry out, complete; make an end of
senses.definition: To bring a purpose to completion; of a life, to bring it to its end.

evidence.note: Of Cyrus: “He is my shepherd, and shall carry out all my pleasure.”
He “carries out the counsel of his messengers”.
“He carries out what is appointed for me.”
Hezekiah: “From day to night you make an end of me”; again 38:13.

stems.gloss: be made to be at peace

senses.definition: Once: the wild beasts brought to be at peace with the man God delivers.

evidence.note: “You shall be in league with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field shall be at peace (הָשְׁלְמָה) with you.”

evidence.locator: Psa.50.14, שַׁלֵּם → ἀπόδος; Psa.62.13, תְשַׁלֵּם → ἀποδώσεις; ἀποδίδωμι renders the verb ×21

evidence.note: “You shall perform (ἀποδώσεις) to the Lord your oaths”: the law of paying vows (Deu 23:22; Psa 50:14).
God “will render to each according to his works”: Psa 62:13.
“Repay (ἀποδιδόντες) no one evil for evil”: Pro 20:22.

evidence.locator: Gen.44.4, שִׁלַּמְתֶּם → ἀνταπεδώκατε; Pro.25.22, יְשַׁלֶּם → ἀνταποδώσει; ἀνταποδίδωμι renders the verb ×25

evidence.note: Job 41:3 from the Hebrew: “and it shall be repaid (ἀνταποδοθήσεται) him”.
“You will be repaid at the resurrection of the just.”
“It is just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you.”

evidence.locator: Exo.21.37, יְשַׁלֵּם → ἀποτείσει; 2Ki.4.7, שַׁלְּמִי → ἀποτείσεις; ἀποτίνω renders the verb ×23, most of them the restitution laws of Exo 21–22

evidence.note: “I, Paul, write it with my own hand: I will repay it (ἀποτίσω)”: making good Onesimus’ wrong.

words.summary: Nearly always plural, שְׁלָמִים, often in זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים “sacrifice of peace offerings”; once singular (Amo 5:22). Its fat was burned on the altar, the breast and right thigh went to the priests, and the rest was eaten by the offerer and his household before Yahweh, the one offering whose flesh the worshipper ate. Scripture does not explain the name; its uses join it to the root’s two chief senses, peace with Yahweh at his table and the paying of vows.

senses.definition: A sacrifice of cattle, sheep or goats, without blemish, whose fat was Yahweh’s, whose breast and thigh were the priest’s, and whose flesh the offerer ate in cleanness on the day or the next; brought for thanksgiving, for a vow or freely, and at the feasts, the covenant and great days of rejoicing.

evidence.note: “If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings … he shall offer it without blemish before Yahweh.”
“This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings”: for thanksgiving, eaten the same day (7:12–15); for a vow or freewill, eaten that day and the next (7:16).
“The person who eats the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings that belong to Yahweh, having his uncleanness on him, that person shall be cut off.”
“The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution I have taken from the sons of Israel from the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and given them to Aaron the priest.”
“Whoever offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh to fulfil a vow or as a freewill offering … it shall be perfect to be accepted.”
“Peace offerings are with me; today I have paid (שִׁלַּמְתִּי) my vows”: the offering and the verb side by side.
“You shall sacrifice peace offerings and eat there, and rejoice before Yahweh your God.”
At the covenant young men offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings; the elders “saw God, and ate and drank” (24:11).
At שָׁבוּעוֹת, the feast of weeks, “two male lambs a year old for a sacrifice of peace offerings”, the only peace offering the feasts of Lev 23 prescribe.

“In the day of your gladness, and at your appointed feasts and new moons, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings, and they shall be a memorial for you before your God.”
The Nazirite completing his vow brings a ram for peace offerings.
Each tribal prince’s gift at the dedication of the altar ends with peace offerings; Shelumiel’s is Num 7:41.
Saul made king: “they sacrificed peace offerings … and Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.”
At the dedication of the house, 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep for peace offerings.
At Hezekiah’s Passover they ate the feast seven days, “sacrificing peace offerings and giving thanks to Yahweh”.
In Ezekiel’s temple the prince’s freewill peace offerings.
“The peace offering (שֶׁלֶם) of your fatted beasts I will not look at”: the singular, refused from a people without justice.
“Are not those who eat the sacrifices partakers of the altar?”: Israel eating of what was offered.

parallels.note: “Burnt offering”: the two named together, the whole burnt and the eaten.

words.gloss: whole, complete, full; undivided (heart); at peace, safe
words.summary: Whole, with nothing cut away or lacking: uncut stones for the altar, a full and just weight, a full measure of sin or of captives, and above all a heart wholly with Yahweh. Twice it is to be at peace with someone, or safe and sound.

senses.definition: Of stones, whole as they came, untouched by iron; of a people, intact in strength.

evidence.note: “You shall build the altar of Yahweh your God of whole stones.”
“An altar of whole stones, on which no man has lifted up iron.”
The house was built “of stone made whole (finished) at the quarry”, no tool heard in it.
“Though they are whole (שְׁלֵמִים) and many, even so they shall be cut down.”

senses.definition: Of a weight, full and honest; of a measure, a reward or a captivity, full with nothing lacking.

evidence.note: “A whole and just weight you shall have, a whole and just ephah.”
“A false balance is an abomination to Yahweh, but a whole weight is his delight.”
“The iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.”
“May your reward be full from Yahweh.”
Gaza “carried away a whole captivity, to deliver them up to Edom”; again of Tyre (1:9).
“So the house of Yahweh was complete.”

senses.definition: A heart wholly given to Yahweh, not divided with other gods; the measure by which the kings of Judah are judged.

evidence.note: “Let your heart be whole with Yahweh our God, to walk in his statutes.”
“His wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not whole with Yahweh his God, as was the heart of David his father.”
“Nevertheless the heart of Asa was whole with Yahweh all his days.”
Hezekiah: “I have walked before you in truth and with a whole heart”; again Isa 38:3.
“Serve him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for Yahweh searches all hearts.”
The people gave willingly “with a whole heart”.
“The eyes of Yahweh run to and fro through all the earth, to show himself strong for those whose heart is whole toward him.”
Amaziah “did right in the eyes of Yahweh, but not with a whole heart”.
The men of war came to Hebron “with a whole heart” to make David king.

senses.definition: At peace with others; safe and sound after a journey.

evidence.note: “These men are at peace (שְׁלֵמִים) with us.”
“Jacob came שָׁלֵם to the city of Shechem”: safe, as he had vowed to return בְשָׁלוֹם (Gen 28:21); or “to Shalem, a city of Shechem”.

greek.gloss: whole, entire, complete in every part

evidence.locator: Deu.27.6, אֲבָנִים שְׁלֵמוֹת → λίθους ὁλοκλήρους; Jos.8.31 the same

evidence.note: “That you may be perfect and entire (ὁλόκληροι), lacking nothing.”
“May your whole (ὁλόκληρον) spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless.”

words.summary: The city of Melchizedek, king and priest of God Most High, whom Hebrews reads as “king of peace”; the psalm sets it beside Zion as Yahweh’s dwelling.

senses.gloss: Salem, the city of Melchizedek, Zion
senses.definition: The name of Melchizedek’s city, which the psalm uses for Zion and Hebrews explains as “peace”.

evidence.note: “Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.”
“His tabernacle is in Salem, and his dwelling place in Zion.”
“First, by interpretation, king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, that is, king of peace.”
“You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.”

words.summary: Scripture’s Aramaic for שָׁלוֹם, used only in the greetings of royal letters.

senses.definition: The wish for welfare that opens a letter.

evidence.note: Nebuchadnezzar “to all peoples, nations and languages … May your peace be multiplied.” Again Darius, Dan 6:26.
Artaxerxes’ answer to Rehum: “Peace.”
“To Darius the king, all peace.”

words.summary: What is paid back: Yahweh’s retribution, and, of corrupt judges, the payment they ask for.

senses.definition: Yahweh’s repayment of a people for what they have done.

evidence.note: “A day of vengeance to Yahweh, a year of recompenses for the cause of Zion.”
“The days of visitation have come, the days of recompense have come.”

senses.definition: A payment asked by a judge for his verdict.

evidence.note: “The prince asks, and the judge asks for a payment (בַּשִׁלּוּם).”
“From the Lord you will receive the recompense (ἀνταπόδοσιν) of the inheritance.”

words.gloss: be finished; (haphel) bring to an end, deliver in full
words.summary: Scripture’s Aramaic verb of the root: a building not yet finished, a kingdom brought to its end, temple vessels handed over in full.

senses.definition: Of a building, completed.

evidence.note: “From that time until now it has been building, and it is not finished (שְׁלִם).”

stems.gloss: bring to an end; deliver in full

senses.definition: To finish a kingdom: God has counted its days and ended it.

evidence.note: “MENE: God has numbered your kingdom and finished it (וְהַשְׁלְמַהּ).”

senses.definition: To hand over the whole of what was entrusted.

evidence.note: “The vessels given to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver in full (הַשְׁלֵם) before the God of Jerusalem.”

words.summary: Once, in the Song of Moses, where Yahweh claims recompense as his own. Paul and Hebrews quote the verse.

senses.definition: The repayment of the wicked, which belongs to Yahweh.

evidence.note: “To me belongs vengeance and recompense (וְשִׁלֵּם), at the time their foot slips.”
“Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord”: Deu 32:35.
The same verse, with “the Lord will judge his people” (Deu 32:36).
ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, “I will repay”.

words.summary: Once, plural, beside שֹׁחַד “bribe”: the payments Jerusalem’s rulers chase. Akkadian šulmānu, a greeting-gift and also a bribe, is the same word.

senses.definition: Gifts given to rulers to win their favour, set beside the bribe.

evidence.note: “Everyone loves a bribe (שֹׁחַד) and runs after payments (שַׁלְמֹנִים); they do not judge the fatherless.”

words.summary: Once: the repayment of the wicked, seen by the one who trusts in Yahweh.

senses.definition: What the wicked receive back for their deeds.

evidence.note: “Only with your eyes shall you look, and see the recompense of the wicked.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܫܠܡܐ (šlāmā), for εἰρήνη: the peace Christ gives, the greeting of his disciples, and “go in peace”.

senses.definition: Peace from God through Christ, and the greeting that wishes it, as in the Hebrew.

evidence.note: “Peace (ܫܠܡܐ) I leave with you; my peace I give to you; not as the world gives.”
“Peace be with you (שלָמָא עַמכֻון).”
“Ask the peace of the house”: the Hebrew שָׁאַל לְשָׁלוֹם.
“Go in peace (זֵלי בַּשלָמָא).”
“Blessed are the makers of peace (עָבדַּי שלָמָא).”
“Let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus the Messiah.”
“King of שָׁלִים, which is king of peace (ܫܠܡܐ)”: the Syriac shows the city and the word together.
“When they say, Peace and quiet.”

words.gloss: pay, fulfil; (aphel) hand over, deliver up; (ethpaal) be delivered up
words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܫܠܡ: the pael is to pay what is owed, as Hebrew שִׁלֵּם; the aphel is to hand over, deliver up, used of handing on the teaching and of Judas delivering up Jesus; the ethpaal, Jesus “delivered up” for our sins.

senses.definition: To pay to God what was sworn, as the law of vows commands.

evidence.note: “You shall pay (תּשַלֵם) to the Lord your oaths.”

senses.definition: To hand a thing or a person over to another: tradition delivered to the believers, and Jesus delivered up by Judas.

evidence.note: “Judas Iscariot, who delivered him up (דַּאשלמֵה).”
“I received from our Lord what I delivered (דַּאשלמֵת) to you: that our Lord Jesus, in the night in which he was delivered up (דּמֵשתּלֵם) …”

senses.definition: Of Jesus, handed over to death.

evidence.note: “After two days is the Passover, and the Son of man is delivered up (מֵשתּלֵם) to be crucified.”
“Who was delivered up (אֵשתּלֵם) for our sins and rose for our justification.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܡܫܠܡܢܐ (mašlmānā), from the aphel “deliver up”: Judas, who delivered up his “man of peace” (Psa 41:10; Jhn 13:18).

senses.definition: One who hands another over to his enemies.

evidence.note: “Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor (מַשלמָנָא).”

cognates.gloss: be safe, secure, free from evil; be free from fault or blemish; sālim, salīm safe, sound, whole
cognates.note: Lane’s sources gloss سَلِمَ مِنَ العَيْبِ as “free from fault, defect, imperfection, blemish”, the wholeness of the Hebrew adjective and qal; قَلْبٌ سَلِيمٌ is a sound heart, as the Hebrew לֵב שָׁלֵם.

evidence.note: “He was, or became, safe, or secure; or he escaped; or he was, or became, free … from evils of any kind … free from fault, defect, imperfection, blemish, or vice.”
“i. q. سَالِمٌ, which means Safe, secure, or free, from evils of any kind”; also of a heart, بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ.

cognates.gloss: safety, freedom from defect or evil; the greeting “peace be on you”
cognates.note: The noun is used as the Hebrew שָׁלוֹם is, both as well-being and as the greeting سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ; form II سَلَّمَ عَلَى is to greet with it.

evidence.note: “Safety, security, immunity, or freedom, from faults, defects, imperfections, blemishes, or vices … سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ is an announcement of the continuance of سَلَامَة.”
“التَّسْلِيمُ … The saluting, or greeting, one with a prayer for his safety … by saying سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ.”

cognates.gloss: peace, reconciliation; one at peace with another; sālama make peace with
cognates.note: Form III سَالَمَهُ “he made peace with him” and the saying “I am سِلْمٌ to whoever is at peace with me” match the Hebrew hiphil “make peace with” and the qal participle שׁוֹלְמִי “one at peace with me” (Psa 7:5).

evidence.note: “Peace, or reconciliation … a man, a woman, who makes peace, or is at peace, with another … أَنَا سِلْمٌ لِمَنْ سَالَمَنِى.”
“He made peace, or became at peace or reconciled, with him.”

cognates.gloss: hand over, deliver to; deliver a deposit to its owner; aslama pay in advance; give up (to an enemy)
cognates.note: Handing over in full what is due to its owner is the act behind Hebrew שִׁלֵּם “pay”; giving a man up to his enemy is the Peshitta’s aphel “deliver up”, used of Judas.

evidence.note: “سلّم إِلَيْهِ الشَّىْءَ He gave to him the thing; or delivered it to him … سلّم الوَدِيعَةَ لِصَاحِبِهَا He delivered the deposit to its owner … أَسْلَمْتُهُ and سَلَّمْتُهُ I left him in the power of him who desired to kill him.”
“أَسْلَمَ is syn. with أَسْلَفَ [as meaning He paid in advance, or beforehand].”

cognates.gloss: be(come) whole, intact, healthy, safe; be completed; (D) complete, carry out in full, pay in full, compensate
cognates.note: One verb carries both the qal’s “be whole, finished” and the piel’s “pay in full, make good”, as in Hebrew.

evidence.note: “be completed; be(come) intact; be(come) safe; be(come) compensated; carry out in full; compensate; fulfil; pay in full; pay off in full; receive full payment; repaying; restoration.”
“completion; final payment.”

cognates.gloss: intact, whole, sound, safe; correct, honest, sincere

evidence.note: “complete; correct; honest; intact; sincere; sound; true; undamaged; well; whole.”

cognates.gloss: completeness, well-being, health, safety; peace; greeting
cognates.note: Akkadian letters open by wishing and asking after the addressee’s šulmu, as Hebrew asks לְשָׁלוֹם.

evidence.note: “completeness; greeting; greeting gift; health; intact state; peace; safety; salutation; well-being.”

cognates.note: The same formation as שַׁלְמֹן (Isa 1:23), and used in the same bad sense.

evidence.note: “bribe; dedication; gift; greeting-gift; present.”

cognates.gloss: be(come) at peace, reconciled; make peace; salīmu peace, reconciliation, divine favour
cognates.note: Akkadian writes this verb with s, not the š of šalāmu, so it stands apart from the regular correspondence; its sense is exactly the Hebrew hiphil’s.

evidence.locator: armep x000038530, salāmu [be(come) at peace] V
evidence.note: “alliance; appease; be(come) at peace; be(come) reconciled; make peace; reconcile.”
“divine pardon; favour; peace; reconciliation.”

cognates.gloss: be intact, healthy, in order, at peace; (D) give peace, well-being; šlm peace, well-being
cognates.note: Ugaritic letters wish yšlm lk, “may it be well with you”, the greeting of the Hebrew.

evidence.note: yšlm “to be intact/healthy, in order, at peace”; D tšlmk “to give peace/well-being”; šlm /šalām-/ “peace, well-being”.

cognates.gloss: peace offerings (?); gifts for obtaining peace
cognates.note: Ugaritic ritual texts name šlmm among offerings, as Hebrew names שְׁלָמִים; and in the Keret epic šlmm are gifts sent to obtain peace.

evidence.note: pl. šlmm (KTU 1.14 III 26, 27) “gifts for obtaining peace”; šlm sing., pl. šlmm (KTU 1.115:9; 1.109:10) “peace-offering(s)(?)”, compared with Hebrew šəlāmîm.

cognates.gloss: greet; fulfil (a vow); compensate; pay back in full; surrender, deliver in payment; keep safe
cognates.note: Punic votive stelae say šlm ʾt ndrm “he has fulfilled his vow”, the Hebrew שִׁלֵּם נֶדֶר word for word; a Phoenician letter uses it of paying back a loan in full, and a decree of compensating those who served.

evidence.note: “v. piʿel 1. GREET SOMEONE … 2. FULFILL a vow, KAI 115.1/2 … 3. … COMPENSATE, KAI 60.6/8 … 4. PAY BACK in full, KAI 50.3/6 … 5. SURRENDER, DELIVER someone/something in payment … 6. KEEP ONE SAFE AND WELL (in personal names).”
“[Heb. šillum] n.m. DELIVERY, SURRENDER: See Š-L-M, ‘surrender, deliver’.”

cognates.gloss: peace, peaceful relations; submission; prosperity, well-being
cognates.note: Azitawadda “made peace (šlm) with every king” (KAI 26), and Punic letters open “may you be well (kn šlm)”.

evidence.note: “n.m. 1. PEACE, specifically PEACEFUL RELATIONS, KAI 26 A I 11/12 … 2. PEACE, specifically SUBMISSION, SURRENDER … 3. PROSPERITY, WELL-BEING … 4. In the expression K-N ŠLM, BE WELL, PROSPER.”

cognates.note: The Marseilles sacrificial tariff sets an animal “cut in pieces” against one šlm kll, “entirely intact”.

evidence.note: “adj. WHOLE, COMPLETE, INTACT, KAI 69.3 (Pu) bʾlp kll ʾm ṣwʿt ʾm šlm kll … ‘whether cut in pieces or entirely intact’.”

cognates.note: Sabaean inscriptions: “they made peace and submitted”; “their war and their peace”; to return from campaign “in health (bslmm)”.

evidence.note: “v pf slmw MAKE PEACE … h pf hslm MAKE PEACE … n slm(m) (1) PEACE (2) SOUNDNESS, HEALTH.”

cognates.gloss: soundness, health, peace; greeting (Targumic and Talmudic Aramaic)
cognates.note: The Targums render שָׁלוֹם by it, including “asking after the welfare” (Targ. Gen 43:27).

evidence.note: “= h. שָׁלוֹם, perfection, soundness, health, peace. Targ. Ps. XXXVIII, 4. Targ. Gen. XLIII, 23 … שאל בש׳ to inquire after the health of; to salute.”

cognates.gloss: complete, perfect, whole, unimpaired; peaceful, friendly

evidence.note: “complete, perfect; whole, unimpaired. Targ. Ex. XII, 5 … Targ. Deut. XXV, 15 … Targ. Deut. XXVII, 6 … peaceful, sincere, friendly. Targ. Gen. XXXIV, 21.”

cognates.gloss: be complete, finished; (pael, aphel) complete, finish, fulfil

evidence.note: “to be perfect, complete, finished, spent. Targ. Ex. XXXIX, 32 … to complete, finish, fulfil. Targ. II Sam. XXII, 26 … Targ. Job XXIII, 14.”

doctrine.statement: Isaiah says of Yahweh’s servant, “the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed” (Isa 53:5); the child given is “Prince of Peace” on David’s throne (Isa 9:5–6); and the ruler from Bethlehem “shall be peace” when the Assyrian comes into the land (Mic 5:1, 4), a verse Matthew applies to Jesus’ birth (Mat 2:6). The apostles say that God preached “peace by Jesus Christ” (Act 10:36), that Christ “is our peace”, who “abolished in his flesh the enmity” and “came and preached peace to you who were far off and to those who were near”, Isaiah’s words (Eph 2:14–17; Isa 57:19), that God made peace “through the blood of his cross” (Col 1:20), and that, justified by faith, “we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ” (Rom 5:1). From the verses: the שָׁלוֹם between God and men that the prophets promised is made in what Jesus suffered in his own flesh, and is offered alike to Israel and to the nations.

Of the Prince of Peace, “of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, on the throne of David and over his kingdom” (Isa 9:6), the throne Gabriel promised to Mary’s son (Luk 1:32–33). The king’s psalm asks that the mountains bring peace to the people, and “abundance of peace till the moon is no more” (Psa 72:3, 7); Zechariah’s king comes lowly on an ass, which the Gospels apply to Jesus’ entry into Jerusalem, and “he shall speak peace to the nations, and his dominion shall be from sea to sea” (Zec 9:9–10; Mat 21:5). “The meek shall inherit the land and delight themselves in abundance of peace” (Psa 37:11), which Jesus repeats (Mat 5:5). Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High (Gen 14:18), is in Hebrews “king of righteousness” and “king of peace”, the pattern of Christ’s priesthood (Psa 110:4; Heb 7:1–2). From the verses: the peace promised is a kingdom on David’s throne, with Christ as king and priest in Salem, and the earth as the inheritance of the meek.

To Cyrus Yahweh says, “I am Yahweh, and there is no other; besides me there is no God … I form light and create darkness, I make peace (שָׁלוֹם) and create evil (רָע); I Yahweh do all these things” (Isa 45:5–7). Amos asks, “Shall there be evil in a city and Yahweh has not done it?” (Amo 3:6), and Lamentations, “Out of the mouth of the Most High do not evil and good come?” (Lam 3:38). From the verses: peace and calamity alike come from the one God; scripture sets no second power over against him as the source of evil.

Yahweh says, “To me belongs vengeance and recompense (שִׁלֵּם)” (Deu 32:35), and he “repays each man according to his work” (Psa 62:13). So his people are told, “Do not say, I will repay evil; wait for Yahweh, and he will save you” (Pro 20:22), and to feed a hungry enemy, “and Yahweh will reward you” (Pro 25:21–22). Paul joins these: “Repay no one evil for evil … do not avenge yourselves … for it is written, Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord”, and then quotes Pro 25:21–22 (Rom 12:17–21); God “will render to each according to his works” (Rom 2:6). No one can put God in his debt: “Who has first given to me, that I should repay him?” (Job 41:3; Rom 11:35). From the verses: because repaying belongs to God, the believer leaves it to him and does good to his enemy.

“When you vow a vow to Yahweh your God, you shall not delay to pay it … but if you refrain from vowing, it shall be no sin in you” (Deu 23:22–23); “better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay” (Ecc 5:3–4); “pay your vows to the Most High” (Psa 50:14). Jesus cites the same law, “you shall pay to the Lord your oaths”, and then tells his disciples not to swear at all but to let their yes be yes (Mat 5:33–37). From the verses: what is promised to God is a debt to be paid in full, and the safest course is to promise only plainly and keep it.

The peace offering was the one sacrifice the worshipper ate: Yahweh’s portion burned, the priest’s given, and the rest eaten “before Yahweh” with rejoicing (Lev 7:11–15, 31–34; Deu 27:7); at the making of the covenant the elders “saw God, and ate and drank” (Exo 24:5, 11); and anyone who ate it in his uncleanness was cut off (Lev 7:20–21). Paul sets the Lord’s table beside it: “The cup of blessing … is it not the sharing of the blood of Christ? The bread … the sharing of the body of Christ? … Consider Israel after the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices partakers of the altar?” (1Co 10:16–18), and warns that whoever eats unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord (1Co 11:27–29). From the verses: the breaking of bread stands where the peace offering stood, a meal of fellowship with God on a sacrifice offered, to be eaten in remembrance and in cleanness.

note: BDB lists the verb’s tokens twice, under v.ds.aa (vb) and v.ds.ad (vb. denom., “be in covenant of peace”); the entry names v.ds.aa only, and keeps the peace senses as stems of the one verb. v.ds.ae (adj.) and v.ds.af (Salem) share the שָׁלֵם tokens of the “whole heart” verses and Gen 14:18, 15:16, 33:18; v.ds.af’s 19 tokens are mostly the adjective, Salem itself being Gen 14:18 and Psa 76:3 (Gen 33:18 may be either). v.ds.ag (noun שִׁלֵּם) and v.ds.ah (the name Shillem) both take Gen 46:24 and Deu 32:35; the noun is Deu 32:35 only. m.dw.af and m.dw.ag are BDB cross-references with no tokens. Proper names of the root not written here, each for its own name entry: שְׁלֹמֹה Solomon (v.ds.at; 1Ch 22:9 ties the name to שָׁלוֹם), שַׁלּוּם Shallum (v.ds.am), מְשֻׁלָּם Meshullam (v.ds.ao), שְׁלֹמוֹת / שְׁלֹמִית Shelomoth, Shelomith (v.ds.au, v.ds.av), שֶׁלֶמְיָה(וּ) Shelemiah (v.ds.az), מְשֶׁלֶמְיָה(וּ) Meshelemiah (v.ds.aq), שִׁלֵּם Shillem and the gentilic שִׁלֵּמִי (v.ds.ah, v.ds.ai), מְשִׁלֵּמוֹת / מְשִׁלֵּמִית Meshillemoth (v.ds.ap, v.ds.ar), מְשֻׁלֶּמֶת Meshullemeth (v.ds.as), שְׁלֹמִי Shelomi (v.ds.aw), שַׁלּוּן Shallun (v.ds.an), שַׁלְמָן Shalman (v.ds.ba) and the Assyrian שַׁלְמַנְאֶסֶר Shalmaneser (v.ds.bb; Akkadian Šulmānu-ašarēd, the god Šulmānu’s name). אַבְשָׁלוֹם and יְרוּשָׁלַםִ are keyed under other roots (a.ae.bb, xj.ak.ae). Leads not yet followed: Ge’ez salām “peace” (Dillmann, no local copy; page not checked); the Peshitta’s ܫܘܠܡܐ “end, fulfilment” and ܫܠܡܘܬܐ “concord” (SEDRA lexemes 3226, 3230) not yet traced to verses. The Septuagint’s σωτήριον for שְׁלָמִים has no New Testament use of the offering, so no Greek is recorded for שֶׁלֶם. Arabic سَلَم “payment in advance” (Lane p. 1414) is a further commercial use of handing over, cited under ar-sallama.
